independent.summary: The stored loss lists are silently truncated at MAX_STORED_URLS=200 while a crawl can lose up to MAX_PAGES=500, so the dashboard panel rebuilt from entity.lastScrape renders "Not learned — 200 pages" for a run that actually lost more; the truncation is only visible in a backend log line, never in the UI the owner reads.

seedFromEntity only guards against an in-flight scrape it knows about (scraping.value), but onScrapeProgress flips scraping to true without clearing scrapeResult — so a scrape started elsewhere (another tab, or a 3am LeoRefresh with the page open) shows the live "Scraping in progress" header above the previous run's seeded "Not learned" list, which now reads as the current run's losses.

triageGrades.reason: No auth, permission, or allowlist code is modified; the new field is server-written and deliberately kept out of the PATCH allowlist.
The only .env.example addition is a log-verbosity knob with a code default, not a credential.
Nothing in the diff touches Stripe, quotas, plans, or pricing.
No delete/drop/wipe is introduced in production code — the one overwrite is of the single latest-run subdocument it owns.
No outbound HTTP, Anthropic, Voyage, Twilio, or Resend call is added or changed.
The new Entity field is optional with no required/unique and the env var defaults in code, so no migration or deploy-config step is required.

summary: The local model reported nothing and the change is in fact sound — both backend write paths (manual full/force and persistRescrapeResult, shared with LeoRefresh) are covered, the field is correctly excluded from the PATCH allowlist and included in the full entity payload — so its empty report is defensible, but it also surfaced none of the two low-severity truncation/staleness issues and its triage, while all correct, carries no evidence.
